brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: 3 full bases at level 1 (piece:0,0,1;full, piece:1,0,1;full, piece:2,0,1;full) with full top covers forming a ~453x310mm deck (f20); dressed with book-row and book-stack props, both visible in look; meshClash clear.
drawer:0#0,1#cut on piece:0,1,0;half-s and drawer:0#1,1#cut on piece:1,1,0;half-s; two half-s bases forming drawer level.

No tool verifies strength; configurator checks fit/collisions only and parts are 3D-printed in user-chosen material. Build is kept low (2 storeys), 3 cells wide, with capOpenFaces and lockJoints applied, but no load rating can be claimed.

finish.summary: Built a low 5-base shelf (3 full cells on level 1 with covers as shelf top, 2 half-s cells below carrying 2 drawers), locked and capped, dressed with a row and a stack of books. Load rating cannot be verified in the configurator.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
